web_evidence.title: Extract: The Leopard, Giuseppe Tomasi Di Lampedusa
web_evidence.note: Penguin's authorized Chapter One extract sustains external narration of the Prince, his family, servants, and setting in third person.

web_evidence.title: Il modello del romanzo storico ottocentesco (University of Florence course slides)
web_evidence.note: The academic structural overview explicitly identifies a heterodiegetic, omniscient narrator and outlines all eight parts; changes in focal character are not changes of narrator person.

web_evidence.title: Il Gattopardo: una rivoluzione senza fine perché tutto rimanga com'è
web_evidence.note: This University of Virginia article in Carte Italiane distinguishes the omniscient narrator from Don Fabrizio and explains that the narrator renders the Prince's thought stream and addresses the reader.

web_evidence.title: The Narrative Instance in Giuseppe Tomasi di Lampedusa's The Leopard
web_evidence.note: The scholarly article analyzes the novel's narrator discourse, free-indirect style, and absorbed interior monologue, treating the Prince's voice as embedded within a distinct controlling narrator.

web_evidence.title: The Leopard (unattributed full-text PDF mirror)
web_evidence.note: Used only for local attribution: q01087 appears inside Don Fabrizio's spoken anecdote to Chevalley, after which the text returns to third-person narration; the mirror's provenance is too weak for primary structural support.

person_note: The controlling narrator is heterodiegetic and omniscient, using third-person narration while frequently adopting Don Fabrizio's and other characters' internal perspectives through free-indirect discourse. The sustained event quotations independently show this external access to characters' thoughts and futures. First-person forms in the dialogue quotations belong to characters; specifically, q01087 is an anecdote spoken by Don Fabrizio, not an alternate narrator. Authorized opening prose and multiple whole-book academic analyses agree, and targeted searches found focalization shifts but no sustained first- or second-person base sections. The only scope limitation is that the authorized publisher extract covers the opening, offset by the whole-book scholarly evidence.
